method: six parallel review agents over the diff since the last audit baseline (19f54bd, 2026-07-25), each finding verified against source and, where it actuates hardware, against the live rig; every fix validated by planting the bug its test exists to catch; full suite green on the w541 (731 passed) and deployed.
surface_reviewed: stockrom.py dump path + rpcops dump worker
rpcops.py routing rework + webapp body parsing

fixed.mechanism: Cache TTL compared wall-clock time (frozen panel across an NTP step-back) and stamped the cache BEFORE the refresh ran (a slow refresh wrote an already-part-expired entry, churning back-to-back refreshes).
fixed.fix: time.monotonic() throughout; stamp at the end of the refresh.

fixed.mechanism: _refreshing event was set before Thread.start(); a start() failure (thread exhaustion) left it set forever, freezing the panel unmarked-stale until restart. The check-and-set was also unlocked on a threaded server, double-spawning workers.
fixed.fix: Clear the event on a failed spawn; check-and-set under _lock.

fixed.mechanism: read_until decoded each recv() chunk separately; a multibyte UTF-8 char split across a 4096-byte boundary became U+FFFD. Markers are ASCII so framing survived; only field content (a non-ASCII hostname) mangled.
fixed.fix: Buffer raw bytes, decode once the ASCII marker is found.

fixed.mechanism: The unit suite's node fixtures carried the real cluster IPs and summary() ran the SSH temp sweep against them, so the suite logged into the e15/p14s/w541. Module-global cache/temp state was never reset, making results order-dependent. The shell-agnostic-probe test asserted only on the _TEMP_INNER constant, never that node_temp wraps it in sh -c.
fixed.fix: autouse reset of module state; stub refresh_temps where fixture IPs are live; assert the constructed remote command is sh -c wrapped.

fixed.mechanism: Each watch entry is two <tr>s in one html string (the visible row and a hidden <tr class=lr> carrying id=log-<slot>). reconcileRows kept only tmp.firstElementChild, dropping every log row. With no log-<slot> in the DOM, doFl/doRemap/_openOnboard all hit `if(!box)return` — flash and single-port onboarding did nothing from the UI, silently, since 2026-07-22.
fixed.fix: Keep each key's whole group of nodes; new test runs the real reconcileRows under a DOM shim.

fixed.mechanism: An empty `function doDump(s){}` sat below the real doDump; JS hoists the last declaration, so the stub won and the Dump mmcblk0 menu item did nothing. DEFINED_FUNCS is a set, so the handler test could not see the duplicate.
fixed.fix: Remove the stub (keep the deliberately-disabled doRestoreDump stub); new static test rejects any function declared twice.

fixed.mechanism: hold() overwrote any existing lock and release() popped it. A dump on a watch mid-wanze-run replaced the 14-day wanze lock and deleted it on release, leaving the run exposed to housekeeping and, because probing() keys on kind, invisible in the UI.
fixed.fix: Refuse to displace a live lock of a different kind (checked and written under _config_lock); watch.dump and probing_set surface the refusal. Same-kind re-hold still renews; expired locks block nobody.

fixed.mechanism: serial (device-supplied ro.serialno / USB iSerial) and dest were interpolated raw into a `bash -c` string; a metacharacter would break the dd redirect or inject a command running as the service user.
fixed.fix: shlex.quote serial and dest, the pattern already used elsewhere.

fixed.mechanism: The one-shot _ssh_align_cycled marker was cleared on ANY non-ssh state. The recovery cycle itself drops the watch to adb_state=None for seconds and busts the status cache, so a poll ran in that window and re-armed the marker — a dead SSH stray then cycled VBUS every few minutes forever.
fixed.fix: Re-arm only on positive recovery (adb_state == 'device'); absence is not recovery. SSH-side recovery re-arms on its own positive evidence.

fixed.mechanism: The size preflight reads over w.t (the live transport) but the copy command re-derived the address from cfg via ssh_ip_for_serial. An orbit/WiFi watch reaches a-d-b on an SshTransport with no ssh_ips allocation, so the copy fell back to an adb command against a watch not on adb — 0 bytes after a preflight that passed.
fixed.fix: Take the ip from w.t, the transport that answered the preflight.

fixed.mechanism: A truncated or crashed dump left its bytes as <name>.img, indistinguishable from a complete one in a directory listing; the only completeness marker was the sidecar manifest, which can be lost — the original-sprat.img failure one step later.
fixed.fix: Rename an incomplete image to <name>.img.partial on both the truncated and exception paths.

fixed.mechanism: There is no cross-port serialization of healing actuations. When N strays or N fake-power-wedged ports cross their thresholds in one pass (fleet cold-boot into developer mode with no leases; ~60s after a restart), one daemon thread per port is spawned within milliseconds and uhubctl_cycle fires N ports near-simultaneously — the adb-crash/brownout the binding 'never many ports at once' rule exists to prevent.
fixed.fix: One shared usb.recovery_cycle_lock held for the whole off->on by every AUTOMATIC recovery cycle (fake-power heal, SSH-stray recovery, adb's wait_serial_online recovery), so they actuate strictly one at a time. Deliberately NOT held by uhubctl_cycle itself, so an operator cycle or onboarding sweep stays immediate. Concurrency test asserts peak overlap of 1; a wiring test pins that adb shares the same lock.

fixed.mechanism: The oplock protects against the three automatic housekeepers (peeler, aligner, fake-power heal — all guarded and tested) but NOT: the CLI check-charge timer (separate systemd-timer process, cuts VBUS unattended, F1); flash.start (F2); charge/drain/workbench Operation.start (F3); the onboarding sweep (F4); the manual mode-switch ops ssh.switch_adb / watch.switch_ssh (F5); maybe_heal_wedged_adb's kill-server (F6); wear.set (F7). port.set already refuses a held watch; a charge that does strictly more does not — the guard is inconsistent at the same API surface. The dump feature is unproven on hardware so most are latent, but the CLI timer runs continuously.
fixed.fix: Wired the lock into every remaining actuator: Operation.start (charge/drain/workbench, one symmetric place for all three), flash.start (via _refuse_if_busy, which also gave it the cross-op check it lacked), the CLI check-charge timer (reads `held` from /api/status - it is a separate unattended process the in-process guards cannot see), the adb wedge self-heal (defers kill-server, which severs an exec-out dump), and wear.set / ssh.switch_adb / watch.switch_ssh. Guarding watch.switch_ssh also closed the aligner's own TOCTOU in finish_ssh_relocation. Each guard has a planted-bug-validated test with a positive control.
fixed.still_open: The onboarding sweep (oplock F4) is deliberately NOT guarded - see the sweep entry in `open`.

open.status: surfaced - needs moWerk's call (changes bulk-operation semantics)
open.mechanism: sweep_prepare cuts VBUS on EVERY leaf port unconditionally and _sweep_one_port powers watches off, with no oplock check. A sweep run while a wanze probe or a dump is live anywhere on the rig ends it. Unlike the other actuators this is explicitly operator-confirmed ('I will power ALL sockets OFF now'), so refusing or skipping changes what the operator asked for.
open.recommendation: Skip held ports and report them in the sweep log, rather than refusing the whole sweep - a watch under a 14-day wanze run is exactly the one not to power off, and the operator may not know it is running. Left for moWerk because it alters a bulk operation's contract.

open.status: surfaced — contained fix, needs UI regression testing
open.mechanism: esc() escapes only & and <, not " or '. Several values interpolate into attribute values and single-quoted onclick JS strings: icecc node hostname (from the remote scheduler), watch serial/codename (device-supplied, several sites raw with no esc), and the Bluetooth advertised device name (attacker-controlled by any nearby radio, in btPair). A crafted BT name or hostname with a quote breaks out into markup or the JS string and runs on click.
open.recommendation: Extend esc() to also escape " and ' (an attribute-safe superset, harmless in text nodes) and esc the currently-raw serial/codename onclick sites, or move onclicks to data-attributes + delegated listeners. Test all UI render paths after — it touches many interpolation sites.

open.status: surfaced — pre-existing, not from this sprint
open.mechanism: Transport routing consults the warmer's fastboot cache (refreshed only when >60s old, skipped while the bus is busy). A watch that just left fastboot is still routed there — `fastboot -s` hangs to a 20s timeout while the watch is live on adb; a watch that just entered fastboot isn't listed yet and reads as unreachable. Window up to one warmer cycle.

webstatus evicts every _watch_os entry whose serial is not currently adb-'device' on each status build, so for an offline watch `detected` is None and _stale_cc keeps the cache. A beluga restored to Wear OS then shelved still shows its old AsteroidOS kernel/Qt/version blob (stale-dimmed) — the exact false claim commit 494c9ad set out to eliminate, for offline watches.
open.recommendation: Persist the detected OS family alongside the cached blob so an offline watch's panel reflects its last known real OS.

open.mechanism: _config_lock is a threading.Lock (in-process only), but the CLI is a separate process doing read-modify-write save_config — a cross-process lost update can drop a live op_lock. And ConfigManager.save truncate-writes in place with no tmp+rename, so a crash mid-write leaves invalid JSON that makes load raise everywhere (fails closed — housekeeping also stops — but the whole service and status page break with no recovery path).
open.recommendation: Atomic config write (tmp + os.replace); consider a flock or moving op_locks to their own atomically-written file.

open.mechanism: No host free-space check before starting an ~8 GB write; a full disk yields a short dump (now caught and marked .partial) and can starve other services sharing the disk.
open.recommendation: shutil.disk_usage(DUMP_ROOT).free >= expect guard before taking the lock.

open.mechanism: The _dump_runs running-check and the assignment are unlocked on a threaded server. Two starts within one second both pass and get the same second-granular dest; interleaved dd writes can still total expect_bytes and be manifested complete.
open.recommendation: A lock around the check-and-claim; the oplock same-kind rule does not stop a second dump because both are kind 'dump'.

open.mechanism: The per-port status loop has no try/except; a pure-Python raise inside it (registry.note / save_config on a full disk) escapes to the dispatcher backstop and the whole status document becomes an error — every watch disappears from the UI, recurring every 2s while the cause persists.
open.recommendation: try/except per port row (log + degrade the row) or around the registry/cache writes on the status path.

open.status: surfaced — likely the unfinished half of the dump/oplock UI
open.mechanism: webstatus emits `held` per port but the UI never reads p.held; a watch held for a dump shows a normal row and every action is refused by the backend with no advance indication. Pairs with the (now-fixed) dead doDump as the unfinished dump UI.
open.recommendation: Render a held badge from p.held, describing kind + age.

open.agent_ref: oplock F13, webstatus F4, rpcops F12
open.mechanism: No test asserts that the power-affecting ops actually CALL _refuse_if_busy (deleting the call fails nothing — the same shape as the flash gap). fb_draining's test asserts a LastSeen round-trip, not the flag condition, so any clause inversion passes. No test drives a request through the bottle handler, so the body-reading layer that failed on hardware is still only tested around.
open.recommendation: An op-table-driven wiring test (every power-affecting op refuses on a held fixture); extract fb_draining into a testable helper; a WSGI-level request test for merge_op_args and malformed-body handling.

open.mechanism: icecc: stale-served slot numbers unmarked; torn cache read (benign). oplock: wall-clock TTL (NTP step can expire/extend a live lock); a falsy `until` reads as immortal (only via a hand-edited entry). webtemplate: literal \n in the sweep-log header; mroomTemp label rounds while the colour class uses the raw value (99.5C shows '100C' in warm colour); two hubs renamed identically drop a header row; dead code (needPwr arg, mkpwr). rpcops: a recovery-mode watch is refused with a false 'not reachable' message; oplock.set accepts an unbounded ttl and ttl:0 silently becomes the default; watch.dump treats any non-'status' action as 'start'. stockrom: disk_bytes matches NO_ROOT on any 'denied' substring.

dropped_suspicions: icecc SSH command injection via node ip — ip is regex-constrained to [0-9.]; _TEMP_INNER!r is valid single-quoted shell.
icecc _refreshing stuck after a worker EXCEPTION — the worker's try/finally clears it correctly; only the pre-start window leaked (fixed).
stockrom restore gates reaching a flash — gpt_gate/fingerprint_gate/restore_plan are sound but have no executor wired yet; refusal paths verified.
merge_op_args precedence redirecting a serial — URL serial/action are authoritative and test-pinned; the real gap was malformed-body handling.
_ssh_delivered miscounting a poweroff that drops the link — deliberate and test-pinned; the gap is the port.poweroff SSH path that does not call it (folded into guard-coverage).
machine-room hidden-contract for null vs [] vs missing — correct and tested.
fake-power oplock guard test being decoration — it now arms every precondition with a positive control; the historical defect is fixed.
